label: unrelated
point: Held that awarding the full invoice value for a delayed seasonal shipment under the Carmack Amendment was general, not special, damages because the carrier kept the salvage value.
change: Restructured subsection (f) on household goods carriers, adding full value protection and released-rate waiver rules.
why: The change concerns household goods movers' liability limits, not damages for commercial shipments that the decision addressed.

label: unrelated
point: The opinion (in a separate opinion) cites 18 U.S.C. 2113 in passing as an example of a statute with an intent element while construing the carjacking statute's intent requirement.
change: Replaced a specific $1,000 fine with 'fined under this title' in one paragraph of 2113.
why: Section 2113 was cited only in passing; the fine change has nothing to do with conditional intent. The report names a different Holloway case (7th Cir. 1993).

label: unrelated
point: Applied the PSLRA pleading standards in 78u-4(b)(1)-(2) to decide whether the complaint adequately pleaded falsity and scienter.
change: Added 78u-4(b)(3)(D) allowing federal courts to stay discovery in state-court actions to prevent circumvention of the discovery stay.
why: The report lists this decision among scienter-pleading cases, but the law changed only the discovery-stay provision, not the pleading standard the court applied.

label: override_express
point: Held that 3729(a)(2) requires proof the defendant intended the false record to get a claim paid or approved by the Government, and (a)(3) requires an agreement to that end.
change: FERA rewrote (a)(2) to cover a false record or statement 'material to a false or fraudulent claim' and (a)(3) to cover conspiracy to commit any violation, dropping the 'to get ... paid or approved by the Government' language.
why: The new words remove the intent-to-get-Government-payment requirement the Court adopted, and the committee report expressly says it corrects Allison Engine.

label: related
point: Held the descendants' claims to the 1972 judgment fund time-barred under 28 U.S.C. 2401(a); 1300d-4(a) was described as the apportionment of the fund.
change: Changed 'plus accrued interest' to 'plus interest received (other than funds otherwise distributed ... under the 1998 Act)' and reworked the distribution under the 1998 Act.
why: The 1998 Act responded to the Loudner litigation by redistributing the fund, but it did not change the limitations/accrual rule the decision applied; the report names this decision as background.

label: unrelated
point: Affirmed a conviction for aggravated sexual abuse of a child in Indian country under 1153 and 2241(c).
change: Added 'felony child abuse or neglect' to the list of offenses in 1153(a).
why: Sexual abuse was already a listed offense; adding child abuse or neglect does not touch the decision's points on sufficiency and sentencing.

label: unrelated
point: Affirmed a conviction under 18 U.S.C. 2252A for receiving child pornography and upheld the CPPA; 2252 was not the provision applied.
change: Raised penalties in 2252(b) (mandatory minimums, higher maximums) and added predicate offenses.
why: The report names Fox only as one of the circuit cases upholding the CPPA before Free Speech Coalition; the penalty changes to 2252 have nothing to do with the decision.

label: related
point: Held that the lineal descendants' claims to the judgment fund did not accrue until they had reason to know of the fund and its distribution, so they were not time-barred.
change: Made the Secretary's roll of lineal descendants under 1300d-3(b) 'subject to' the 1998 Act, which reallocated the fund, set ancestry verification and channeled challenges to set courts.
why: The Act addresses the same fund and litigation (the report cites this decision), but it does not change the accrual rule the court decided.

label: related
point: Held that the 292(a) false-marking penalty of up to $500 is assessed per falsely marked article, not per decision to mark.
change: Added 'Only the United States may sue for the penalty authorized by this subsection,' ending qui tam suits for the penalty.
why: Congress responded to the qui tam surge the decision caused (the report names it), but it left the per-article penalty rule intact and changed only who may sue.

label: related
point: Upheld a 924(c)(1) 'use' conviction based on loaded pistols kept near drugs on a closet shelf.
change: Restructured 924(c)(1) into graded minimums and added liability for anyone who 'in furtherance of' a drug trafficking crime possesses a firearm.
why: The report cites Crass as an example of pre-Bailey broad readings of 'use'; the new 'possession in furtherance' prong addresses Bailey and would likely still reach Crass's facts, so the decision's result is neither reversed nor its holding codified.

label: override_express
point: Held that tractors are subject to the 4051 retail excise tax regardless of gross vehicle weight absent a will-not-equip certificate, so the light chassis cabs were taxable.
change: Added 4051(a)(4) excluding tractors with a gross vehicle weight of 19,500 pounds or less and gross combined weight of 33,000 pounds or less.
why: The new exclusion reverses the decision's regardless-of-weight rule for light tractors, and the conference report cites this decision as the holding being addressed.

label: unrelated
point: Noted Monterey County's designation as a covered jurisdiction under 4(b) and held the court could not order elections under an unprecleared plan.
change: Changed a cross-reference in 1973b(b) from section 1973d to 1973f (examiners to observers renumbering).
why: The change is a conforming cross-reference; the report cites Lopez only as evidence of section 5 noncompliance.

label: related
point: Held that 5317(c) did not authorize forfeiture for an 'attempted' failure to file a CMIR because 5324(b) does not prohibit attempting to fail to file, and no filing duty had arisen.
change: Rewrote 5317(c) into criminal and civil forfeiture of property involved in a violation of 5313, 5316 or 5324 or a conspiracy, dropping the 'transaction or attempted transaction' language.
why: The rewrite still requires an actual violation or conspiracy, so the decision's conclusion that no violation had occurred would stand; no packet evidence ties it to this case.

label: codifies
point: Held that the proponent of federal jurisdiction need show the amount in controversy by a preponderance of evidence about contested jurisdictional facts, not to a legal certainty.
change: Amended 1332(a)(2) to bar alienage jurisdiction between citizens and permanent resident aliens domiciled in the same State and removed the deeming sentence; the same Act added 1446(c)(2) on the amount in controversy.
why: The committee report cites Meridian approvingly as the source of the preponderance standard written into new 1446(c)(2); the 1332(a) text change itself is unrelated to the decision.

label: related
point: Reviewed VA regulations implementing the 5103 notice and duty-to-assist provisions, invalidating the 30-day response deadline in 38 C.F.R. 3.159(b)(1).
change: Added 5103(a)(2) requiring the Secretary to prescribe by regulation the content of 5103(a) notice, differentiated by type of claim.
why: The report cites the decision only for background on Morton; the notice-content requirement does not change the response-period ruling.

label: related
point: Held SORNA's 2250 'travels' covers only travel after the Act's effective date, citing Jackson's reading of the present-tense 'travels' in 2423(c) by analogy.
change: Amended 2423(c) to reach a citizen who 'travels in foreign commerce or resides, either temporarily or permanently, in a foreign country.'
why: The change addresses the travel element of 2423(c) that the decision used only as an analogy; it does not alter 2250, the provision the decision construed.

label: unrelated
point: Denied a COA because the 2255 motion was untimely under the one-year limitation, rejecting reliance on the 2255 para. 6(4) trigger and equitable tolling.
change: Redesignated the undesignated paragraphs of 2255 into lettered subsections without substantive change to the limitation triggers.
why: Purely structural redesignation; the decision's timeliness analysis is unaffected.

label: related
point: Held Ammex lacked standing under 6427(l) to claim a diesel excise refund because it was not the ultimate purchaser of the fuel.
change: Added a refund route for ultimate vendors of diesel used in certain intercity buses and changed claim timing rules in 6427.
why: The report cites the decision in background on duty-free fuel sales, but the changes do not make a duty-free reseller an ultimate purchaser or otherwise change the decision's 6427(l) result.

label: unrelated
point: Applied the 1101(a)(42) refugee definition in denying asylum to a Malian applicant.
change: Amended the Irish Peace Process program visa category in 1101(a)(15)(Q) and substituted Secretary of Homeland Security for Attorney General.
why: The change is to a different paragraph of 1101(a) unrelated to the refugee definition.

label: related
point: Denied a preliminary injunction on the dilution claim because the parody film was a noncommercial use excluded by 1125(c)(4)(B), even though it tarnished the mark.
change: TDRA rewrote 1125(c) to cover likely dilution by blurring or tarnishment, define both, and restate exclusions including noncommercial use and parody fair use.
why: The rewrite addresses the same dilution provision but keeps the noncommercial-use exclusion (and adds parody), so the decision's result would stand.

label: override_express
point: Held that requests for payment from Iraqi funds administered by the CPA were not FCA 'claims' unless the United States provided the money, rejecting the custodian theory.
change: FERA rewrote 3729(a), removing the requirement that the claim be presented to a U.S. officer, and redefined 'claim' to cover requests for money 'whether or not the United States has title' to it.
why: The new definition reverses the rule that government-administered non-U.S. funds fall outside the FCA, and the committee report names this litigation as wrongly decided.

label: override_express
point: Held that 1759's common-bond requirement unambiguously requires the same common bond to unite every member of an occupational credit union, invalidating NCUA's multiple-group interpretation.
change: Struck the common-bond clause and added 1759(b) expressly authorizing multiple common-bond credit unions, among other membership categories.
why: The new text allows the multiple-group credit unions the Court held unlawful, and the report says the Act responds to this Supreme Court decision.

label: unrelated
point: Held the court lacked jurisdiction over a congressman's interlocutory challenge to a search warrant under the Speech or Debate Clause; 201 was cited only as an offense listed in the warrant.
change: Added definitions of foreign official and a new offense in 201(f) prohibiting foreign officials from demanding bribes.
why: The decision did nothing with the bribery statute's text beyond listing it; the foreign-bribery addition is unrelated.
